text:
Sam: heads up — after merge #3112 we got a canary perf alert. tail latency ~2x, compile-queue exploded, lots of kernel compiles. Looks like the selector picked the new low-cost heuristic and is preferring an int8 path that triggers recompilation churn.

Maria: can you drop logs and a quick summary?

Sam: repro summary: canary traffic -> 99p latency 220ms (baseline 110ms), compile jobs 300/min (baseline 25/min). KV cache miss spiked; eviction rate jumped. snippet:```
[compile-queue] enqueued=312 jobs/min
[autoselect] picked kernel_id=0x7fb int8-fused score_delta=-0.18
[kvcache] evict_rate=8.3x, miss_rate=0.41
```

Jordan: did you bisect to a single commit?

Sam: yes, bisected to PR #3112 (kai/kernel-selector-prefers-low-cost). Rolling it back locally removes the churn.

Kai: yep that was my change — aimed to bias towards cheaper kernels for long sequences. I missed a fallback/hysteresis for recently-compiled kernels.

Maria: can you repro on staging with a stable replay? if so we can run perf counters and pprof.

Sam: repro on a 3-node staging with replay of canary traces: run flags `--seq_target=1024 --batch=1 --replay-rate=1`. Attached short flame output: `hotspot: compile_kernel()` dominated during the spike. Link: https://perf.internal/reports/2145/3112-flame (internal).

ci-bot: canary-checker reported regression at 2026-03-17T10:41:02Z — latency and compile-rate thresholds breached.

Jordan: this looks like a rollout blocker. We should either revert the PR or land a hotfix with hysteresis. Which is faster?

Kai: I can push a tiny patch to add a warm-up bias: prefer recently-successful kernels for 5 minutes and only switch if score_delta < -0.5. Will test locally now.

Sam: sounds good but if hotfix fails we should revert — current canary is hurting other teams.

Maria: I'm +1 for revert to unblock traffic, then follow up with Kai's fix and unit tests. Need a short changelog entry for the revert.

Sam: created revert PR #3121 (revert: kernel-selector-prefers-low-cost). CI: quick smoke passes but we'll watch canary.

deploy-bot: started canary deploy for PR #3121 at 2145003000

Sam: watching metrics — compile-rate dropping back toward baseline.

deploy-bot: canary health update at 2145003200: 1m averages: compile_jobs=28/min, 99p latency=115ms. Thresholds restored.

Kai: thanks — I'll open follow-ups: (1) selector hysteresis patch + tunables, (2) unit tests that simulate KV cache churn and verify selector stability, (3) a perf test in CI that runs long-seq replay to catch regressions.

Maria: please include a targeted perf-test in the PR pipeline (maybe a nightly job) — CI didn't catch this because our short-run perf gate didn't hit compile churn.

Sam: agreed. Also adding a telemetry counter for `selector_switch_count` per model/version so we can alert on oscillation.

Jordan: action items: Kai -> patch + tests (owner). Sam -> telemetry + run a longer nightly replay. Maria -> add revert note and coordinate release. I'll mark this as a rollout-blocker during the incident.

Kai: will send draft PRs by EOD. Sorry team, my change tried to optimize cost but caused instability — learning here is to prefer stability hedges first. :disappointed: 

Sam: no worries. good catch and quick revert. Follow-ups will prevent repeat.

Maria: closing the thread when follow-ups are linked.

Sam: thanks everyone.
